carry_forward_constraints: S23 must not automate any send/submit action from S22 state='approved' alone; verify authorized reviewer, timestamp, per-recipient confirmation, unexpired draft and exact draft/message hash.
Use RFC/IANA-reserved lab domains (.test/.invalid/.example or reserved example.com/net/org); do not reuse @example.pe as a supposedly safe non-routable recipient.
Do not inherit S22 least_privilege_ok as valid: mail.send must fail the draft-only lab policy and requested/granted scopes must be observed, not hardcoded.
Do not treat moving an external recipient to BCC as sufficient to hide internal To/Cc addresses; use individual drafts when required by minimum disclosure.
Do not reuse S22 OrderedDict dedupe or @other.test-only external detection; recipient policy must never increase visibility and must use the actual allowlist.
Approval must be invalidated if the draft expires, recipients/content/subject/attachments change, or the upstream S21 payload changes.
Idempotency must identify the complete canonical message and be enforced atomically; sha256(run|to|body_ver)[:16] is not creditable as a guarantee.
S23 must preserve one persisted audit trail linking S21 payload -> S22 draft -> recipient set -> approval -> browser action; isolated print statements are not provenance.
S21 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED; S23 must not assume the report package or pending_review manifest is reconciled merely because S22 references it.
Do not navigate a real mail provider or real recipient target in course tests; use a controlled test site/sandbox and synthetic reserved addresses.
